name: Holmes's Retirement to the Sussex Downs
description: At some point in 1903 Holmes retires from active practice and moves to a small farm on the Sussex Downs near Eastbourne, devoting himself to bee-keeping and the writing of his Practical Handbook of Bee Culture. The Preface to His Last Bow, written by Watson, confirms the retirement; The Adventure of the Lion's Mane (narrated by Holmes himself) describes his Sussex life directly. Holmes consents to be drawn back into active work twice — for the Von Bork affair in 1914, and for the Lion's Mane investigation in his own neighbourhood. The retirement permanently changes the geography and tone of the late canon.
